To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

KRAS mutations were associated with mucinous histology, high CA 19-9 level, but were not prognostic or predictive for PFS and OS in metastatic colorectral cancer patients receiving first-line chemotherapy with or without Bevacizumumab.
KRAS mutation was significantly associated with high CA 19-9 level, but not with the clinical response to bevacizumabbased therapy or with the prognosis.

KRAS, NRAs, BRAF and Pik3ca mutations are not prognostic factors, but KRAS, NRas, BRAF and pik3ca wild type status is a predictive factor in metastatic colorectral cancer patients receiving first-line FOLFOX ± Bevacizumabe.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of KRAS mutation in metastatic colorectum cancer patients receiving bevacizumbab.
the importance of the expanded KRAS, BRAF mutation testing for the selection of metastatic colorectal patients who will most benefit from the anti-VEGF therapy.
the significance of KRAS mutation in the prediction of the response to bevacizumabbased therapy and the prognostic significance of KRAS, BRAF mutation and PIK3 CA mutation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
patients with KRAS, NRAs, BRAF and/or PIK3CA mutated tumours are not candidates for bevacizumabbased treatment, but further prospective clinical trials are necessary.
KRAS, BRAF or PIK3CA mutant status is not a contraindication for bevacizumabbased therapy in mCRC patients, while NRAS wild type status is associated with better treatment response.

the KRAS mutation analysis is mandatory in the decision making process for anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody therapy and that the expanded KRAS, BRAF mutation and PIK3C4 mutation analysis may be considered in the decision making for bevacizumabb treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
KRAS, NRAs, BRAF and/or PIK3CA mutated patients receiving bevacizu-mab should be considered for anti-EGFR treatment, as they are likely to benefit from it.
KRAS mutation is a predictive factor of response to bevacizumabe treatment in metastatic colorectral cancer patients receiving first-line FOLFOX ± Bevacizumabe therapy.
KRAS and other genes mutation analysis is a useful tool for the selection of patients with metastatic CRC for anti-EGFR targeted therapies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
KRAS, NRas, BRAF and/or PIK3CA mutational status may be a predictive factor for bevacizumabb efficacy.
KRAS mutation is not an absolute exclusion criteria for bevacizumabefficacious treatment.
expanded KRAS, BRAF mutations and PIK3A analysis may provide additional information for treatment decisions.
